title: MLB Logo Quiz Part 3: Hard Mode
headline: MLB Logo Quiz Part 3: Name The Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Logo
description: A hard MLB logo quiz: eight tiny pieces of MLB team logos, about 2% of each logo. Guess the team, tap to reveal the answer, keep score and share your result.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current MLB team logo, about one fiftieth of the whole mark. No full letters, no team names, no giveaways. Each piece still holds one real detail, a color pair, a curve or an edge that belongs to only one team.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

How Every MLB Team Got Its Name

items.piece: A navy serif at the bottom of the K.
items.fact: For years the KC lived only on the cap. In 2014 it went on a regular-season jersey for the first time in franchise history.

items.piece: The bottom left foot of the A: navy outline, red and darker red.
items.fact: The current red A with a halo debuted in 2005, when the club dropped Anaheim from its logo.

items.piece: The orange outline curling around a navy serif at the bottom right.
items.fact: The Mets' colors honor the teams New York lost: blue from the Dodgers and orange from the Giants.

items.piece: Blue, red and black stripes of the M.
items.fact: The marlin looping over an M was unveiled on November 15, 2018. The M echoes the 1950s Miami Marlins and Havana Sugar Kings.

items.piece: Where the navy T crosses the red C.
items.fact: TC stands for Twin Cities. The 2023 refresh redrew it in the same new lettering as the new M logo.

items.piece: The curl at the top left of the red P.
items.fact: The Phillies' red-and-blue look replaced the maroon uniforms they wore in the 1970s and 1980s.

items.piece: The bottom of the P's bowl, gold with a pointed serif.
items.fact: In 2014 the gold P became the Pirates' primary logo, replacing the eye-patch pirate.

items.piece: The end of the green swash at the bottom of the A.
items.fact: The A's green and gold date to 1963, when owner Charlie Finley switched the team to kelly green and gold.
